purpose: The known-defect state of the engine frozen as DEVELOPMENT PRE-VALIDATION BASELINE V3 (cycle 9, §114): every CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM or LOW defect known and not fixed at the freeze, so that an external error can be read later against what was already known. It never removes an error from a metric and never corrects a result retrospectively (§67).
history: The pilot's list (validation/pilot_v1/manifests/known_defects.json, version 2) is not rewritten: it stays the list of the SPANISH PILOT BASELINE and of the ENGLISH VALIDATION BASELINE. This file is the state of V3. An adjudicator may tag an error with any identifier of either file; the tag says the defect was known when the analysis was made, not that it was absent from the baseline measured.
severity_scale: CRITICAL · HIGH · MEDIUM · LOW, the pilot's impact scale (§60); for ordering work, never a score
unresolved_high: KD-28 (TD-14): reader friction, registered HIGH for its breadth; it holds with a question and executes nothing. The false executions still known are MEDIUM (KD-29: a condition written with 'we', split by 'and' or on 'SatO2' runs now).

fixed_before_v3.class: A discharge for later (its own time, after an observation or a result, on a condition) ran now
fixed_before_v3.example: Alta en 2 horas · Discharge home in 2 hours · Observe 6 h then discharge home
fixed_before_v3.tagging: In a run of a frozen baseline, an immediate discharge from a discharge written for later is this defect: known at the time of analysis, present in the frozen baseline (§67).

fixed_before_v3.class: A reassessment in abbreviated hours ran at 0 minutes
fixed_before_v3.example: Reevaluar en 1 h · Reassess in 1 hr

fixed_before_v3.class: A treatment received before the resident's care, told as such, was given again or asked about as the resident's order
fixed_before_v3.example: Epinephrine 0.5 mg IM given by EMS · Aspirina 300 mg dada por SAMU

fixed_before_v3.class: Trauma: after a loss replaced with crystalloid, blood set off the transfusion overload rule
fixed_before_v3.example: Tourniquet + 3 L NS, then 2 U: overload
fixed_before_v3.tagging: Engine physiology, not the reader; the rule it amends (TD-21, principle D) exists from V2 on.

defects.class: 'd/c' and 'dc' are not read as a discharge
defects.example: d/c home · Dc home w/ EpiPen x2 · D/C home 4 hrs post epi if no rebound
defects.what_happens: Nothing is read (the generic notice), or the line is kept as a home prescription and the discharge is lost without a word; with a time or a condition it is a plain conditional, not a disposition plan. 'd/c NS' still stops the fluid.
defects.known_cause: 'd/c' is the fluid-stop verb; as a discharge it is read only in 'OK to d/c'.
defects.why_not_fixed: Found or confirmed in cycle 9 outside the classes it fixed; §90 of the cycle 9 instruction defers MEDIUM and LOW findings, and the reader is frozen at V3 (§112).
defects.pilot_relevance: Silent loss of a discharge in English shorthand; the pilot measures it.
defects.next_step: Class of discharge shorthand, with the fluid 'd/c' as its negative control.
defects.evidence: Adversarial review of cycle 9: D01, D02, D05, D14, D15, D18, D34, H09

defects.class: A discharge written as an intention, a possibility or in the past is neither run nor recorded
defects.example: Plan to discharge home in 2 hours · Planeo alta mañana · Will discharge home tomorrow · Posible alta en unas horas · Discharged home w/ EpiPen · Dada de alta a domicilio · Después de 3 NBZ de salbutamol, PEF 80%: alta · Tras adrenalina IM, PA 120/80 y sin estridor: alta con EpiPen
defects.what_happens: Nothing is recorded; the generic notice asks for an order ('Discharged home w/ EpiPen' keeps only the EpiPen prescription). 'Vamos a dar de alta en 2 horas' is a disposition plan. A bare 'alta' after a colon is not read either.
defects.known_cause: The intention and past forms were not part of TD-39's class.
defects.why_not_fixed: Found or confirmed in cycle 9 outside the classes it fixed; §90 of the cycle 9 instruction defers MEDIUM and LOW findings, and the reader is frozen at V3 (§112).
defects.pilot_relevance: A plan lost without record; the pilot measures it.
defects.evidence: Cycle 9 probes; adversarial review of cycle 9: D06, D13, D25; second review of cycle 9: DA06, DA07

defects.class: An observation or a control written without 'dejar en' is not read
defects.example: Observe 6 h · Observar 4 horas · Control en 1 hora · Control en 30 min · Discharge home, recheck in ED in 24 h · PCP follow-up tomorrow at 0900 · allergy clinic in 4 weeks
defects.what_happens: Nothing runs; the generic notice (or, for a recheck, a question about an unrecognised study). 'Dejar en observación 6 horas' is the ED observation of D4. Some follow-ups written after the discharge are dropped from the record.
defects.known_cause: Only the D4 form of an observation is an order.
defects.why_not_fixed: Found or confirmed in cycle 9 outside the classes it fixed; §90 of the cycle 9 instruction defers MEDIUM and LOW findings, and the reader is frozen at V3 (§112).
defects.pilot_relevance: Silent loss of an observation; the pilot measures it.
defects.evidence: Cycle 9 probes; adversarial review of cycle 9: H11; second review of cycle 9: DC04, DC05 (incidental)

defects.class: After a reassessment, what follows in the same sentence is absorbed
defects.example: Reassess in 30 min, 2 L NS · Reassess in 30 min, discharge if improved
defects.what_happens: The verbless fluid after the reassessment is lost without a word; a reassessment followed by a conditional discharge becomes one conditional plan and the reassessment does not run.
defects.known_cause: The reassessment groups the pieces after it.
defects.why_not_fixed: Found or confirmed in cycle 9 outside the classes it fixed; §90 of the cycle 9 instruction defers MEDIUM and LOW findings, and the reader is frozen at V3 (§112).
defects.pilot_relevance: A fluid lost without a word, or a reassessment that does not run.

defects.class: Interval forms outside hours and minutes
defects.example: Reevaluar en 20' · Reassess in 90' · Reevaluar a las 14 h · reevaluar a la hora · Reevaluar en hora y media · Reassess in 1 h, then every 30 min
defects.what_happens: Minutes written with an apostrophe run at 0 without a word; a clock time after 'a las' is read as an interval in hours (840 minutes), which the engine asks about (0–120); 'a la hora' is asked. 'Hora y media' without 'una', and a first interval followed by a repeat interval, are asked.
defects.known_cause: TD-34 read hours and minutes; the apostrophe and clock times were not part of it.
defects.why_not_fixed: Found or confirmed in cycle 9 outside the classes it fixed; §90 of the cycle 9 instruction defers MEDIUM and LOW findings, and the reader is frozen at V3 (§112).
defects.pilot_relevance: A reassessment at the wrong time, silently for the apostrophe.
defects.next_step: With TD-34's interval reader, if the external data show these forms.
defects.evidence: Adversarial review of cycle 9: R20, R23, R26, H18; second review of cycle 9: RI01, RI05, RI06

defects.class: Repeating or continuing a treatment given before the resident's care
defects.example: Repeat the epinephrine given by EMS · Ya recibió adrenalina, repetir adrenalina 0,5 mg IM · Continue NS started by EMS at 125 mL/h · Salbutamol nebulizado hace 20 minutos en el SAPU, repetir · Otra dosis de adrenalina 0,5 mg IM, ya recibió una en su centro de salud hace 15 minutos
defects.what_happens: The repeat is held with a question ('No matching administered treatment' or 'Specify which recorded drug or fluid to repeat'), even with drug, dose and route written and after the prior dose is recorded; the continuation is read as a bolus that asks its volume. Visible, but it delays epinephrine. A trailing 'repetir' after the recorded history is lost without a word.
defects.location: family_parser / family_engine (repeat of a recorded treatment)
defects.known_cause: A repeat refers to a treatment given in the encounter; a prior treatment is history.
defects.why_not_fixed: Found or confirmed in cycle 9 outside the classes it fixed; §90 of the cycle 9 instruction defers MEDIUM and LOW findings, and the reader is frozen at V3 (§112).
defects.pilot_relevance: A time-critical order held by a question.
defects.next_step: A repeat of a prior treatment as a new order with its own dose.
defects.evidence: Adversarial review of cycle 9: H27, S1–S3, P15, P16, P17, P35, P36; second review of cycle 9: OR06, OR16

defects.class: The second treatment of a prehospital account
defects.example: EMS gave epi 0.5 IM and diphenhydramine 50 mg IV · El SAMU le puso adrenalina 0,5 IM y metilprednisolona 125 mg IV · Prehospital: epi 0.3 IM + benadryl 25 IV · Recibió AAS 250 mg y nitroglicerina sublingual en el SAMU
defects.what_happens: The first treatment is recorded as prior treatment. A modelled second one is not given but is held with a question instead of recorded; a not-modelled one is recorded as the resident's decision (a Trace distortion); after a header and '+', it is dropped. A second prehospital dose of the same drug is not recorded; a prehospital nitroglycerin is not recorded (relevant beside the right ventricle of acs_54m_inferior) or is asked about as the resident's order.
defects.known_cause: The account is split at 'and'/'y'/'+' before the source is read.
defects.why_not_fixed: Found or confirmed in cycle 9 outside the classes it fixed; §90 of the cycle 9 instruction defers MEDIUM and LOW findings, and the reader is frozen at V3 (§112).
defects.pilot_relevance: Nothing is given again; the record of the second drug is wrong or missing.
defects.next_step: The account's list read as one account.
defects.evidence: Adversarial review of cycle 9: P03, P13, H21–H24; second review of cycle 9: PT03, PT04, PT10, PT11
defects.also_seen_in: C8 (the first one was given again)

defects.example: s/p epi 0.3 IM by EMS · Epi IM x1 PTA · El 112 le puso adrenalina y Urbason · Recibio adrenalina IM por el 061 · Trae vía periférica canalizada por SAMU · Methylpred 125 mg given at OSH · Took 4 baby aspirin at home before calling 911 · Tres nebulizaciones con salbutamol en el consultorio antes del traslado · No response to the epinephrine given at urgent care · Adrenalina IM puesta por un amigo en el restaurante

History without a recognised place, participle or 'hace' is missed; some is read as a new order and stopped by a dose question; a friend's EpiPen is recorded as a home prescription.

defects.class: One unrecognised fragment holds every order written with it
defects.example: Epi 0.5 mg IM now, already drawn up · Epi 0.5 mg IM, EMS report reviewed · Epi 0.5 mg IM now, symptoms began 30 min before arrival · Segunda dosis de adrenalina 0,5 mg IM; la primera se la pusieron en el SAPU · Epinephrine 0.5 mg IM, same dose as given at urgent care · AAS 300 mg VO. En casa tomó 100 mg hace 2 horas. · Methylprednisolone 125 mg IV; she took prednisone 40 mg at home this morning
defects.what_happens: The engine asks about the fragment and holds the other orders of the submission, epinephrine included, until it is answered. A history clause the reader cannot classify, written with the order, holds epinephrine, aspirin or the steroid behind a question.
defects.known_cause: A clarification holds the submission by design (59O-03).

defects.pilot_relevance: A time-critical order delayed by a question.
defects.next_step: Prose fragments read as prose, by class.
defects.evidence: Adversarial review of cycle 9: H29, H31, H32, D36, P14; second review of cycle 9: OR03–OR06, OR14, OR17

defects.class: Vocabulary and forms outside the reader, mostly held with a question (TD-14)
defects.example: amp of D50 · epi drip · Narcan · Page GI · STEMI code · floor/pabellón · D5W · glucosalino · run/hang/push · coags · protonix · q15min · titulando a PAM > 65
defects.what_happens: Mostly held with a question (63 of 108 and 19 of 32 in the blind sets of cycle 6): honest, visible, but it costs turns. What of it is lost without a word is KD-26.
defects.known_cause: Vocabulary and forms outside the reader's classes; see docs/REGISTRO_DEUDA_TECNICA.md, TD-14.
defects.why_not_fixed: Registered HIGH for its breadth (friction), not for false executions. §20 of the cycle 9 instruction leaves TD-14 to the external data.
defects.pilot_relevance: Friction the pilot measures; a question never executes anything.
defects.next_step: By class, ordered by the external measurement.

defects.example: EDA urgente para ligadura de várices · IC urgente a cirugía ya · Cuando la SatO2 baje de 92%, iniciar O2 por naricera · Once she has had 30 mL/kg and MAP remains < 65, start norepinephrine · OK to send home · Alta ok · Return to OR if rebleeds

defects.class: A home instruction after the discharge is read as an order now
defects.example: Discharge home, start prednisone tomorrow · Adrenalina autoinyectable para casa
defects.what_happens: The discharge is held by a question about the steroid's dose; an auto-injector 'para casa' without a discharge is read as an epinephrine infusion that asks its rate. Nothing runs by itself.
defects.known_cause: Only 'with/con' and a comma list after the discharge are home prescriptions.

defects.class: The critical-event screening does not cite a recorded prior treatment
defects.example: Aspirin 300 mg given by EMS (ACS) · Epinephrine 0.5 mg IM given at OSH (anaphylaxis)
defects.what_happens: The prior treatment is recorded as history and never given, but the screening's facts for 'no antiplatelet' or 'no epinephrine' do not mention it: the omission is still proposed (for aspirin as a reading) and the faculty member sees the history only in the Trace. No event is ever accepted automatically.
defects.known_cause: The screening reads executed actions; a prior treatment is not one, by design (TD-36 records history, it does not model prehospital care).
defects.why_not_fixed: Found or confirmed in cycle 9 outside the classes it fixed; §90 of the cycle 9 instruction defers MEDIUM and LOW findings, and the reader is frozen at V3 (§112).
defects.pilot_relevance: Faculty confirmation reads it; the proposal can be wrong beside a prehospital dose.
defects.next_step: Cite the recorded prior treatment in the facts, as the withheld orders are, with a faculty decision.

known_behaviour_by_design.class: A discharge after a wait of stated length is a plan, even when the wait is described as uneventful
known_behaviour_by_design.example: Tras 6 h de observación sin incidencias, alta a domicilio · After 6 h of uneventful observation, discharge home
known_behaviour_by_design.why: In a simulation the stated wait has usually not passed; a plan is visible and can be carried out with one more line, a discharge run too early cannot be undone. 'Now/ahora' in the discharge, or a value measured without a threshold before it ('Tras 3 nebulizaciones PEF 80%, alta'), make it a discharge now.

known_behaviour_by_design.class: A time at the end of what a discharge sends home belongs to the discharge
known_behaviour_by_design.example: Discharge home with EpiPen in 2 hours · Alta a domicilio con EpiPen en 2 horas
known_behaviour_by_design.why: It is a plan unless that part names something with its own time (a follow-up, a control, a return, a dose, a start, 'every/cada'): 'Alta con control en 2 horas' discharges now.
